transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well, hello Dr. Smith. I, uh... I came in today mostly 'cause my wife insisted. See, it's about the men down at the domino table, and sometimes that announcer on the radio. They've been giving these little messages that are meant just for me. Warning me to be careful, you know? 

I listen to that radio every single morning. It's an old wooden one, a Zenith, I think. Got it at a hardware store years and years ago when they still sold good appliances. You just don't see craftsmanship like that anymore, everything is all cheap plastic now. My neighbor, he bought a plastic one and the knob broke off in a week. Can't even tune it. 

But anyway, my wife, she says it is all just talk and I'm making it up, but I know they are warning me to be careful. She doesn't listen, though. She was too busy fussing with the garden this morning when I tried to tell her. The tomatoes are coming in real early this year because of the heat. We usually don't get them till late July, but the ground's been so dry...
When you hear these messages on the radio, are you hearing actual voices speaking to you, or is it just that you are interpreting the words of the announcer as being directed at you?

Well, the fella on the radio, he's just talking his regular broadcast talk, you know? But I know what he means. It's his words, but the warning is meant for me. 

But... I suppose sometimes I do hear actual voices, too. Not from the Zenith, no. Like, some afternoons when the house gets real quiet... my wife usually goes to lie down around two o'clock. She's got a bad hip, you know. Needs a replacement but they say she's too old for the surgery now. It's a crying shame, she used to love to go walking down by the creek to look for those little painted turtles. 

Anyway, when it's quiet like that, I'll hear my old friend. He calls my name right from the front porch. Or sometimes he's just out there humming a choir song. It's clear as a bell, like he is standing right there by the screen door. We used to sing in the choir together, years and years ago. He had a deep baritone, could really rattle the pews. The church got a new pastor recently, a young kid from up north. Doesn't even wear a tie on Sundays! Can you imagine that? Standing up at the pulpit in just a regular shirt. I told my wife it ain't respectful for the Lord's house, but she says times are changing and I'm just being stubborn.
Aside from these experiences, how has your mood been lately—have you been feeling persistently down and hopeless, or perhaps unusually energetic and euphoric for weeks at a time?

Well, you know, it's funny you ask about energy. Some weeks, I wake up and I just feel... bright. Like I'm important, you know? I'll be laughing loud, talking a mile a minute. I feel like I could build a whole new shed out back if I wanted to. Speaking of sheds, the hinges on mine are rusting out completely. I told the boy at the hardware store I needed solid brass, but they sold me this cheap galvanized nonsense. It rained for three days straight last April, just poured and poured, and the water got right into the joints. Ruined a perfectly good bag of potting soil I had sitting in there. 

But anyway, when I get like that, feeling all bright and fast... if my wife tries to slow me down or asks me too many questions, I get real sharp with her. I just snap. It's like I don't have the patience for it. She'll be asking me about what we're having for supper, and I'll just bite her head off. We usually have supper around five-thirty, right after the evening news. The fella who anchors the news now, he's got this terrible comb-over. You'd think with all the money they pay those television people, he could afford a decent haircut. My old barber, Frank, he used to give a proper trim for two dollars. Course, Frank passed away back in '98. Heart attack right there in the shop. Such a shame.
When you are not feeling that bright, fast, and energetic way, do you still hear those voices or feel like people are sending you messages?

Well, let me think on that... yes, yes I do. There was a quiet month not too long ago, maybe late autumn. I was sleeping just perfectly normal, going to bed at nine and waking up with the sun, and I wasn't full of all those big plans or feeling fast at all. I usually sleep on my left side, you know, 'cause of my digestion. If I eat green peppers or onions after four o'clock, I get the worst heartburn. My wife makes a wonderful sausage and pepper bake, but I always tell her, you gotta serve it by noon or I'll be pacing the floor all night. 

But anyway, even during that quiet month when my mood was just flat and regular, I still heard my friend out there on the porch. Clear as day. And I still knew that radio announcer was sending me those warnings. 

Speaking of the porch, the paint is peeling awful bad on the west side. We painted it a nice robin's egg blue a few years back, but the sun just beats down on it all afternoon. Fades the color right out. You really gotta use a good oil-based primer if you want it to last, but these days they just water everything down. You buy a gallon of paint now and it's half water, I swear. I was telling the fellow at the hardware store...

You mentioned that even during that quiet month where your mood was flat and regular, you were still hearing those voices and receiving those messages; how many months in total, over the course of your life, have you experienced these voices or messages while your mood was feeling perfectly normal?

Well, let's see now... if I had to put a number on it, I'd say those voices and the special messages, they've been coming and going for about nine months total. Started around the time the weather started getting warm last year. 

Warm weather always brings out the June bugs, you know. They just thud against the screen door all night long. Thud, thud, thud. Drives my wife crazy. She tried hanging one of those bug zappers out by the garage, but all it does is make this awful buzzing sound. Zzzzt. Zzzzt. And it smells like burnt hair, I swear it does. I told her we should just plant some marigolds around the porch, I read in the Farmer's Almanac that marigolds keep the bugs away. My mother used to grow the biggest marigolds you ever saw, bright orange ones. She had a green thumb, that woman. Could stick a dead twig in the ground and make it bloom. She used to make this rhubarb pie in the summer... oh, it was tart, but with a big scoop of vanilla ice cream, it was just heaven. You can't find good rhubarb at the market anymore, it's all stringy and tough...
